practice.development[5]: The booklet asks students to count axes, test a supplied axis, or complete a shape about a supplied axis; it does not ask them to identify an axis from a complete figure. Replace this off-booklet task with a booklet question type at the same tier and update its structure slug.

practice.mastery[2]: The answer is correct, but the solution says the blades curve; the diagram consists entirely of straight segments. Correct that factual description while retaining the symmetry reasoning.

quiz.q6: Option 0 incorrectly says the line has no line symmetry without restricting that claim to the y-axis; option 2 likewise uses unqualified line symmetry. Scope the option wording to symmetry about the y-axis so that only option 0 is correct under the stated tests.

quiz.q8: Option 0 incorrectly claims no line symmetry at all, although the graph has axis x=0.8. Restrict the options' line-symmetry claims to the y-axis; the supplied solution and distractor reasoning correctly address that restricted test.

quiz.q9: Identifying the equation of an axis from a complete parabola is not a question type asked in this booklet. Replace it with an adapted booklet question type under the same quiz id and update its structure slug.

theory: Qualify the parallelogram claim: rectangles and rhombi are parallelograms with reflection axes, so only a parallelogram that is neither has 0 axes. Qualify the final parabola claim: having its vertex on the y-axis alone does not imply axis x=0; the parabola must have a vertical axis. Also distinguish having half-turn symmetry from having order exactly 2: a circle is preserved by a half-turn and by every other rotation.
summary: Replaced practice.development[5] and quiz.q9 with cited booklet question types, updated their structure slugs, corrected the straight-blade description, and restricted quiz.q6 and quiz.q8 option wording to the supplied symmetry tests. Qualified the theory statements about parallelograms, vertical-axis parabolas and half-turn symmetry; no whole items were removed.
reviewSummary: All supplied tasks are booklet question types, and the theory and remaining answers are sound; no worked examples or removals were supplied. Repair the visually ambiguous kite in quiz.q1 and the rounded regular-polygon construction in quiz.q3.
findings: quiz.q1: Make the kite visibly different from a rhombus, or explicitly mark its two unequal pairs of equal adjacent sides. The current unlabelled drawing differs from a rhombus by only $0.05$ units in the vertical distances, so students cannot reliably distinguish the correct $1$ axis from the $2$-axis distractor using the supplied figure.

quiz.q3: Generate the vertices using exact expressions $90+k(360/7)$ for $k=0,\ldots,6$ rather than rounded angles, and identify the shape as a regular heptagon in the question. This makes option index $0$ uniquely correct and supports the solution's regularity assumption.
